summary.name: Open Contexts
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS window switcher that replaces ⌘Tab with a per-window switcher and adds a persistent app bar with saved window groups.
use_cases: Switch between multiple windows of the same app, such as two Chrome windows
Find a window by typing an app name or window title
Organize windows into groups for code, chat, or research
Keep a persistent sidebar of open windows on screen edge
Reach windows on other macOS desktops from one switcher
summary.what_it_does: Open Contexts takes over ⌘Tab so it switches between individual windows in most-recently-used order rather than one icon per app. Holding ⌘ and typing filters the list by app name or window title, with space-separated terms combined. An app bar can sit on the left, right, or bottom of the screen, with icons only or icons plus titles, and supports multiple displays. Users can create, rename, and reorder window groups, and the groups persist across restarts. Groups and window positions are saved locally in a single groups.json file.
notable: Shows every window individually in ⌘Tab, with search by app name or window title
Persistent app bar with saved window groups that survive restarts
Local-first: groups stored in one JSON file, no account or cloud
Written in native Swift with AppKit and SwiftUI; Apache 2.0 licensed
caveats: Needs Accessibility permission; without it ⌘Tab is not taken over
Showing windows from all desktops must be enabled manually in Settings
